# App Title: 

The project we propose it looking at the general global education statistics to see how globally education varies in both who participates, but also the skills which individuals have.

## Lit REVIEW


#Proposed Data:
The data we propose to use come from ![UNICEF]("https://data.unicef.org/topic/education/overview/#data") which is made of 7 separate data sets: out of school rates, adjusted net attendance rates, completion rates, foundational learning skills, information communication technology skills, youth and adult literacy rates, and school age digital connectivity. Within these tables, we can compare by country, region of the world, developmental status, across various education levels, giving percentages of the key topic along with gender, population density as a factor, and by wealth distribution across each stage in education path (primary, secondary) with occasionally looking at pre-primary and adult outcomes. The data also represents a variety of years, which can be filtered to look at an individual country's change over time or how they compare at certain time points.

It appears that each sheet has ~100 countries listed, each with approximately ~15 variables, across 3 sheets in 7 excel files.

#Actor Description: 
Individuals who have an interest in comparing the educational outcomes from different countries to determine where global humanitarian foundations should target their services to improve education for all people of the world.

# Actor Questions of Interest:
- Comparing literacy by country - adult vs children
- Comparing computer skills by country by wealth quintile
- Comparing by country the proportion of students not in school (by development, gender, schooling level, wealth quintile)
- Comparison of reading and numericy skills between two different age groups by country (by development, gender, schooling level, wealth quintile as well)

# Anticipated Actor Workflow:
Dataset of interest (select) -> select countries or global regions -> stop and use that level variables or select sub variables (gender, region, wealth, etc) -> create plots/stats tests
